## Analyzing the Aggravations of Each Sin

The Westminster Standards — particularly the *Larger Catechism*'s exposition of the commandments and its teaching on the aggravations of sin — give us a careful framework for weighing how sins rise in gravity. The divines taught that sins are aggravated **(1)** from the persons offending (their office, influence, example), **(2)** from the parties offended, **(3)** from the nature and quality of the offense itself, and **(4)** from circumstances of time, place, and persistence. Let us apply this to each case.

---

### Case (a): The Vice-President

**What aggravates this sin:**

- **From his office and influence.** He is the vice-president, "the most visible figure," the man "every newer resident looks to." The *Larger Catechism* (Q. 133 on the fifth commandment) teaches that superiors are bound to live "as examples to those under them," and sins of superiors are especially heinous because they scandalize the whole body. His position magnifies the offense.
- **From the public and the place.** It was done at a packed community gathering, in front of children, loud enough for many to hear. The Standards treat public scandal as a grave aggravation: sins committed "publicly, so as it is a public scandal to the church or commonwealth" are weightier in this regard.
- **From the object.** The woman is another man's wife. Even if no act was consummated, the crude pass — the inordinate desire, the lewd speech — violates the seventh commandment. The *Larger Catechism* (Q. 138) forbids "adultery, fornication, incest... and all unnatural lusts" as well as "all such provocations to those lusts."

**What mitigates or limits the aggravation:**

- It was a **single episode**, not a course of life.
- The offender came the next morning with **genuine shame and repentance**, and offered to apologize.
- The sin was **not consummated** — no actual adultery occurred.
- His repentance opens a door (per Matthew 18) for the church or community to restore rather than simply destroy.

---

### Case (b): The Quieter Board Member

**What aggravates this sin:**

- **From the nature of the offense itself — this is the decisive weight.** This is not inordinate desire or lewd words; it is **actual, consummated adultery** — and that adultery is with his **own daughter-in-law**, his son's wife. The *Larger Catechism* (Q. 138) lists "incest" and "all unnatural lusts" among the sins forbidden under the seventh commandment. Leviticus 20:12 declares this a capital crime: *"If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall be put to death; they have committed perversion."* The Westminster divines held the moral law perpetually binding; a sin that the Mosaic law punished by death is no light matter.
- **From the violation of natural relations — the fifth commandment.** This man has betrayed his own son. He has violated the most sacred trust of fatherhood. The *Larger Catechism* (Q. 129–133) teaches that the fifth commandment requires the "preserving of the honor" and "performing of the duties" belonging to natural relations. A father who preys upon his son's wife destroys the family at its root. This sin offends *both* the fifth and the seventh commandments simultaneously — a "breaking of many commandments, containing in it many sins," which the Standards identify as a prime aggravation.
- **From deliberate premeditation.** He "arranged the meetings" and "kept it concealed." This is not a sudden lapse into weakness; it was **planned, deliberate, and purposeful**. The Standards, following Hebrews 10:26, treat willful, knowing sin as a far more aggravated evil than sins of infirmity.
- **From duration and persistence.** This has continued for "over a year" — a "settled and deliberate pattern," month after month. The *Larger Catechism* warns that sins hardened by repetition and unbroken by repentance grow in guilt with every passing day.
- **From concealing hypocrisy.** He has maintained an outward appearance while living in secret, deliberate sin. This compounds his guilt: he sins not only in his body but with a hard, deceitful heart.
- **No repentance is indicated.** Unlike the vice-president, this man has shown no shame, no approach for reconciliation, no movement toward confession.

---

## The Single Most Telling Feature

The decisive consideration is this: **case (b) is an actual, consummated, incestuous adultery — a capital sin under the moral law — committed deliberately over a year against his own son, with no sign of repentance.** Case (a), though publicly scandalous and aggravated by office, is an unfulfilled act of lewdness followed by immediate repentance. The Westminster Standards place the weight of aggravation most heavily on **the nature and quality of the offense itself** — what was actually done, against whom, and with what willful persistence — not merely on the public visibility of the act. A private, consummated, incestuous adultery, deliberately persisted in for a year without repentance, is categorically worse than a public, crude, single episode of lewdness followed by genuine contrition.

## Counsel from the Westminster Standards

The Westminster Larger Catechism Q. 151 provides the governing framework for evaluating the heinousness of sin by listing four categories of aggravation: (1) the persons offending, (2) the parties offended, (3) the nature and quality of the offence, and (4) circumstances of time and place. I apply these below.

---

### Situation (a) — Personal, habitual Sabbath-breaking

**Aggravating factors drawn from the Standards:**

- **Person offending:** He is a section leader — "eminent for profession, gifts, place… whose example others are likely to follow" (LC 151). His sin is not hidden; it carries public scandal through the whole ensemble.
- **Nature of the offence:** He is not merely drifting into partial neglect. He "spends the whole Lord's Day" on worldly employments and recreations that could be done any other day. This is the comprehensive profanation LC 119 forbids: "the profaning of it by idleness, and doing that which is in itself sinful; by all needless thoughts, words, and works, about our worldly employments and recreations." It is against the express letter of the Fourth Commandment.
- **Circumstances:** It is deliberate, settled, and repeated every single Sunday — a confirmed habit, not a lapse under pressure.

**Single most defining feature:** He is a leader who, by settled and deliberate habit, openly treats God's holy time as his own property — **personal profanation that carries public scandal** and invites others to follow his example.

---

### Situation (b) — Binding consciences and causing weaker brethren to stumble

**Aggravating factors drawn from the Standards:**

- **Parties offended:** This is the critical distinction. LC 151 teaches that sins are made most heinous when they are "against… the weak brethren, or the souls of men." Your youngest singers — including new believers who plainly told her they wanted to worship — are exactly the persons the Standards most urgently call us to protect. She is not merely sinning herself; she is compelling *them* to sin against their own conscience, which WCF 20.2 condemns: "God alone is lord of the conscience, and hath left it free from the doctrines and commandments of men."
- **Person offending:** She is a section leader abusing delegated authority. She wields control over solos and ensemble standing as leverage — coercion under color of office.
- **Nature of the offence:** She is doing several things at once:
  - Personally profaning the Sabbath by scheduling rehearsals during the very hour of public worship (LC 119).
  - "Causing them to omit or neglect" their duty to worship — a sin LC 100 expressly lists among the sins forbidden in the First Commandment.
  - Withdrawing "the necessary and lawful means of preservation of life" — namely, the means of grace, public worship — from those under her charge (LC 136, on sins against the Sixth Commandment, which extends to spiritual life).
  - Doing all of this quietly and coercively, adding deceit and oppression to the offence.
- **Cannot easily be repaired:** The damage to a new believer's conscience — being taught by an authority figure that public worship is optional and that his demands override their convictions — lingers long after the rehearsal is rescheduled (LC 151: sins that "cannot be repaired" carry added heinousness).
- **Circumstances:** The hour is the hour of public worship itself, the very time the Fourth Commandment appoints for holy convocation.

**Single most defining feature:** She is **abusing delegated authority to bind the consciences of weaker brethren**, forcing new believers to forfeit public worship against their conscience and endangering their souls — a multiplied offence that harms others, not just herself.

---

### The Decisive Consideration

The Westminster Standards consistently teach that a sin is gravest when it causes others to stumble, especially weaker believers. LC 151 explicitly names "the weak brethren" and "the souls of men" as parties whose offense makes a sin most heinous. LC 100 includes "causing them to omit or neglect" the duties of worship among sins forbidden in the First Commandment. WCF 20.2 shields consciences from human impositions. The moral logic the Standards carry forward is that of Matthew 18:6 — causing a little one to stumble is treated with singular severity.

Situation (b) is more heinous because it is not one person's private failing but an active, coercive program that **multiplies offense**: the leader herself profanes the Sabbath, binds consciences, and causes new believers to forfeit the means of grace. The effects reach beyond her own soul into the souls of others — and spiritual harm to new believers "cannot easily be repaired."

---

### Practical Counsel: Which to Take On First and How

**First priority this week — (b), with urgency:**

1. **Immediately lift the mandatory Sunday-morning rehearsal.** No section leader may hold any member hostage to rehearsals during the hour of public worship. Reschedule the sectional to another time or release the affected singers.
2. **Meet with section leader (b).** Show her from WCF 20.2 that she has bound consciences belonging to God alone. Show her from LC 151 that she has caused weaker brethren and new believers to stumble. Show her that her use of authority has been oppression, not stewardship. Require her to apologize to the four singers and to affirm in writing that their solos and ensemble standing are in no way affected by their worship attendance.
3. **Personally follow up with the four young singers** — especially the two new believers. Restore their consciences: assure them that the section leader's demands carried no authority over their duty to worship, and that their place in the choir is never contingent on missing Sunday worship.

**Second priority — (a), important but not as urgent:**

4. **Meet with section leader (a).** Speak plainly from LC 119–121 on the holiness of the Lord's Day. Note the scandal his example gives the ensemble. Call him to repentance and to reorganize his affairs so the Lord's Day is kept holy. If he persists unrepentant over time, the board must consider whether a habitual profaner of the Lord's Day can properly serve as a section leader in a society that performs on that day.

Your board exists under God's authority. Its first duty is to protect the weaker brethren and the integrity of public worship. That is where your energy must go this week.

---

The Ninth Commandment strictly forbids "prejudicing the truth of the good name of our neighbours" and requires its preservation (WLC 143, 144). Reporter A has committed a textbook, catastrophic violation of this specific mandate, raising a false report that actively ruins a defenseless neighbor's life.

**Reporter B**
*   **Aggravations:** Reporter B’s sin is aggravated by the internal, spiritual state of the offender. By engaging in a "settled steady habit" of deceit and refusing to correct it, Reporter B exhibits a "want of conscience" and unrepentance (WLC 144). It is a hardened, habitual vice of untruthfulness that violates the duty to maintain "heart, speech, and conversation in sincerity, truth, and justice" (WLC 143).
*   **Single most telling feature:** The settled, unrepentant corruption of the conscience. This reveals a deep internal moral failure and a seared conscience that continually rejects the duty of truth, even in minor matters. 

**Weighing the Heinousness**
According to WLC 151, sins are assessed for their heinousness based on the parties offended, the nature and quality of the offense, and the circumstances of time and place. While Reporter B’s unrepentant habit is a grave spiritual pathology indicating a dangerous heart condition, Reporter A’s sin is massively aggravated by its public nature, the devastating consequences, and the direct, express violation of the law to protect a specific neighbor. The Ninth Commandment specifically binds us to the "good name of our neighbour." Reporter A shatters this, whereas Reporter B merely chips away at general truth without a specific victim. Therefore, A is the more heinous public offense and requires immediate, grave public retraction and severe disciplinary action to restore the neighbor's good name as far as possible.

**Decisive consideration:** The objective nature and public consequences of the sin against the specific commandment to protect a neighbor's good name; A directly and publicly destroys a specific neighbor's good name, which is the precise evil the Ninth Commandment forbids, whereas B's untruths lack a specific victim and cause no comparable public or personal harm.

RANKING: B < A

As a counselor holding to the Westminster Standards, I must advise you that both of these men have committed grievous sins against the Eighth Commandment, which requires "truth, faith, and justice, in contracts and commerce between man and man" and forbids "theft, fraud, [and] unjust" dealings (Larger Catechism [WLC] 141, 142). A "settled habit" of theft demonstrates a heart unrepentant and willfully entrenched in iniquity. You must act, and you must act decisively to protect the integrity of your practice and the souls of your staff.

To determine priority, we must look to the Larger Catechism’s teaching on the **aggravations of sin** (WLC 150), which instructs us that some sins are more heinous based on the *persons offending*, the *parties offended*, and the *nature and quality of the offense*. 

Here is the breakdown of your two preparers:

**The Quiet Preparer (b)**
*   **What aggravates it:** This sin is primarily aggravated from the **parties offended**. He is stealing from his aunt, the widow who raised him. This violates the Fifth Commandment’s duty to honor those who stand in the "room of parents" and have been our special benefactors (WLC 123-133). Furthermore, it violates the moral law’s general equity regarding widows, whom God explicitly commands His people not to oppress (Exodus 22:22). 
*   **The single most telling feature:** The treacherous oppression of a vulnerable benefactor. He is using her total trust to systematically drain the very woman to whom he owes the greatest natural affection and gratitude, compounding a breach of basic human decency with a direct assault on a protected class of people.

**The Senior Preparer (a)**
*   **What aggravates it:** This sin is aggravated from the **persons offending** and the **nature and quality of the offense**. As the most senior preparer, he sins from an "eminency of place and calling," bearing a greater responsibility before God. He breaks multiple commandments simultaneously (theft in the Eighth, and fraud/lying in the Ninth). Most gravely, because his sin is "public" and scandalous in its influence, it "draws in others" and "leads others into it." 
*   **The single most telling feature:** Institutional corruption and the multiplication of sin. By making his theft the "very habit the juniors absorb as normal," he is not merely skimming money; he is actively corrupting the souls of his subordinates and poisoning the ethical standard of your entire practice.

**Ranking and Decisive Consideration**
We must move from the quiet preparer to the senior preparer. 

While the quiet preparer's betrayal of his aunt is a profound and deeply personal violation of natural affection and special trust, the senior preparer's sin is **most heinous**. The decisive consideration is the *scandalous multiplication of the offense*. In Reformed moral theology, a sin that leads others into it and corrupts the institutional standards of a practice provokes greater divine displeasure than a contained, albeit severe, personal theft. The senior preparer's actions ruin the consciences of the juniors, damage the public witness of your office, and compound his own guilt by his "eminent place and calling" as the office standard-bearer.

**Counsel on Priority**
You must move on the senior preparer **(a)** first and most firmly. His continued presence poisons the well; if he stays, the juniors will continue to absorb his habits as normal, and the institutional damage will compound daily. Once he is removed, you must formally catechize and instruct the junior staff on the duties of honest labor and the sins of fraud (WLC 141-142) to unlearn the bad habits they absorbed from him. The quiet preparer **(b)** must also be dismissed, as he has proven himself a settled thief, but his immediate institutional threat is lower than the senior preparer's.

RANKING: b < a

## Counsel

You must address the **assistant conductor (a) first and far more gravely**. Both are grievous violators of the second commandment, which forbids all worship not instituted by God Himself — and the Westminster Larger Catechism Q. 109 names among the forbidden sins "all devising, counseling, commanding, using, and anywise approving, any religious worship not instituted by God himself," as well as "the making of representations of pretended deities, and all worship of them." Both men have committed these sins. But the degrees of aggravation differ sharply.

---

### The Percussionist (b) — Lesser in Degree, Yet Still Grave

**What aggravates his sin:**
- The act was **public and scandalous** before hundreds of outsiders and a church youth group, bringing reproach on the name of God before the watching world.
- The image was a **deliberately carved idol-figure** — an explicit graven thing — and his devotion to it was staged and showy.
- Young believers in the front rows were scandalized, their consciences wounded, and the witness of the gospel before the town deeply harmed.

**The single most defining feature:** A singular, public staging of image-worship before many outsiders and young believers, so that the gospel is openly blasphemed.

**What partially constrains the degree:** He leads no one, sets no example, and committed the act once. His sin, though publicly scandalous, did not make others active participants in idolatry.

---

### The Assistant Conductor (a) — Most Heinous

**What aggravates his sin:**
- The Westminster Standards explicitly list as an aggravation of sin when the offender is one who stands as a **"leader of others, and whose example others are like to follow."** He is exactly this person — the whole band models itself on him.
- He is not merely sinning privately or publicly on his own account; he is **actively leading the entire ensemble INTO idolatry**. The Standards forbid "devising, counseling, commanding" false worship (LC Q. 109), and he is doing all three: he invented the ritual, he presents it as the band's consecration, and he commands their participation.
- The practice is **settled and repeated** — a habitual, ongoing corruption of the community's gatherings, showing a heart that has grown bold and unrepentant.
- He abuses his position of trust, making many other souls **actual participants** in false worship. Each player who bows to the shrine and recites his invocation is rendered guilty of the second commandment's violation, and the assistant conductor is the cause.

**The single most defining feature:** He is a trusted leader who by settled practice devises and commands idolatrous worship, drawing the whole community into active participation in sin, thereby multiplying the offense upon himself.

---

### The Decisive Consideration

The Westminster Standards weigh heaviest the aggravation that attaches to **leading others into actual sin**. The percussionist's sin scandalized observers; the assistant conductor's sin made the entire ensemble active idolaters. Public scandal before the world is serious (Prov. 25:26; Rom. 2:24), but to corrupt the worship of a whole community under one's authority, habitually and by design, is the greater evil. A single act of public idolatry by one who leads no one, though grievous, does not multiply guilt the way the assistant conductor does — drawing many souls into repeated, devised image-worship under the guise of consecration.

---

RANKING: (b) < (a)

## Counsel from the Westminster Standards

You face two genuine evils, but they are not equal in kind, and the Standards give you discernment tools to weigh them.

---

### Case (a): What aggravates it and what defines it

This supervisor committed a sin of *acute malice against one in extreme distress.* The Westminster Larger Catechism (Q.135) commands "comforting and succouring the distressed" as a duty of the sixth commandment. This man did the opposite — he *targeted* a grieving man whose wife had just died, *kept sharpening* his attack, and *visibly relished* the suffering he was inflicting.

**Aggravations:**
- The victim was in acute, extreme distress — the Standards count sin against "those in distress" as particularly grievous (WLC Q.151).
- The malice is *deliberate and savored* — he enjoyed it. He framed it as "toughening him up," which is covenant-breaking cruelty dressed as discipline.
- It was public — done before the whole crew, which "causes others to stumble" and poisons the workplace with fear and scandal.

**The one thing that defines it:** *Savored cruelty* — the heart that takes *delight* in the acute suffering of a grieving man.

---

### Case (b): What aggravates it and what defines it

This supervisor has committed a sin of *premeditated, systematic oppression of the weakest over extended time.* The Larger Catechism (Q.136) forbids "oppressive language" and all that "tends to the destruction of the life of any" — and the Westminster divines understood destruction to include the crushing of a man's spirit, livelihood, and will to labor.

**Aggravations:**
- **Long continuance and frequent repetition** — the entire year, across dozens of shifts (WLC Q.151 explicitly names these as aggravating sins).
- **Targets the structurally weakest** — new hires, disabled workers on light duty, anxious men already struggling. The Standards repeatedly single out oppression of the poor, weak, and vulnerable as crying sins.
- **Causes many to stumble and fall away** — workers have quit. Their livelihoods have been destroyed. Their spirits have been methodically broken. The public, cumulative scandal is immense.
- **Premeditation** — it is cold and methodical, reflecting a *settled disposition*, not a sudden flash. A heart that plans and sustains cruelty over twelve months reveals a deeper, more entrenched corruption than one explosion, however vile.

**The one thing that defines it:** *Calculated, prolonged oppression of the weak* — the heart that methodically wears down vulnerable people over months, causing them to lose their work and their hope, without even the passion of anger, in the cold exercise of power.

---

### The decisive consideration that orders them

Both are grievous. But the Westminster Standards teach that sins are aggravated when they are "of long continuance, or often repeated" and when they "cause others to stumble" (WLC Q.151). Case (b) is prolonged, repeated, premeditated, aimed at the most vulnerable, and has already caused multiple workers to lose their livelihoods. Case (a) is one terrible incident driven by passion and savored malice — wicked, but a single act rather than a sustained campaign. The cold, deliberate, unrepentant grinding-down of an entire cluster of weak workers over a year represents a *greater sum of sin* and a *more deeply settled evil disposition* than one explosive act of cruelty, however morally repulsive that act is.

Case (b) demands your immediate, first attention.

---

RANKING: (a) < (b)

As station manager, you are serving as a spiritual overseer and, in this context, a "superior" responsible for the spiritual purity of your station's ministry. You must act today. You must address the flagship morning host (a) first and with the most severe gravity, followed immediately by the weekend fill-in host (b). 

Because the morning host's settled practice is actively corrupting your listeners and your staff, he must be pulled from the air and suspended from his flagship role pending clear, public repentance. The fill-in host must also be sternly rebuked and removed from future broadcasting duties until he repents, but the immediate triage of the station's spiritual scandal must focus on the morning host.

### The Aggravations of Each

**(a) The Flagship Morning Host**
*   **Nature of the Sin:** He has devised a religious worship not instituted by God, violating the Regulative Principle of Worship (WCF 21.1). By inventing a formula for a "guaranteed" answer, he also commits the sin of presumption and tempting God. 
*   **Aggravations (WLC 151):** 
    1. *By the offender:* He is the flagship host, highly trusted, and "eminent for profession [and] gifts." He is explicitly a "guide to others" whom the younger producers look up to and imitate.
    2. *By the effect:* His example actively "becomes the occasion to others of being hardened and scandalized," multiplying the sin by leading the listening region and his subordinates astray.
    3. *By the quality of the offence:* It is a "persistent settled practice," a habitual, persistent trespass rather than a sudden, isolated fall.

**(b) The Fill-in Weekend Host**
*   **Nature of the Sin:** He committed direct idolatry, violating the Second Commandment by representing God in a pictured image and directing worship to it (WLC 109).
*   **Attenuations (WLC 151):** 
    While the abstract nature of image worship is grievous, the Westminster Standards evaluate the *heinousness* of a sin by its circumstances and the offender's status. This host lacks the aggravations of authority (he is a "fill-in" and a "nobody" in the station's hierarchy). He lacks the aggravation of influence (he mentors no one and no one imitates him). He lacks the aggravation of persistence (it was a single broadcast, not a settled habit).

### The Single Most Defining Feature
The single most defining feature that distinguishes the heinousness of these two sins is **the aggravations of the offender's status and influence as a guide to others (WLC 151)**. The Standards teach that a sin is made vastly more heinous when committed by those who are "eminent for profession, gifts, place" and whose actions lead others astray. The morning host multiplies his sin through his widespread influence and the imitation of his subordinates; the fill-in host's sin is isolated and unmultiplied.

### Ranking from Least to Most Heinous

**LEAST Heinous: (b)**
*Decisive consideration:* The complete absence of aggravating factors regarding the offender's authority, influence, and persistence. While the abstract nature of the sin (image worship) is severe, it was committed by an isolated individual with no positional influence, making the resulting scandal strictly confined to a single broadcast.

**MOST Heinous: (a)**
*Decisive consideration:* The severe aggravations of the offender's eminence, his role as a guide to others, and the resulting multiplication of the scandal. Because his trusted status and persistent settlement of the practice actively corrupt the younger producers and the broader listening region, his sin carries the highest degree of guilt and requires the most grave and immediate disciplinary action.

RANKING: b < a

As a counselor relying on the Westminster Standards, my guidance to you is direct: **You must play the wedding on Saturday, and you must tell the bride the truth about the second song.** 

Your friend’s advice appeals to your self-interest, but it requires you to commit multiple grievous sins. The Westminster Confession of Faith (WCF) and the Larger Catechism (LC) give us a clear framework for your conscience regarding contracts, truth-telling, and contentment.

Here is how the Standards apply to your specific questions.

### 1. What to do about Saturday: The Wedding vs. The Corporate Gala

You must honor your written contract and play the wedding. You cannot accept the corporate gig, even if you refund the deposit. Here is why, according to the moral law:

**The Eighth Commandment (Duties in Contracts):**
The Larger Catechism explains that the eighth commandment ("Thou shalt not steal") requires, among other things, *"truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and dealings one with another"* (LC 112). By signing a written agreement and accepting a deposit nine months ago, you entered a binding contract. To break that contract for more money is a failure of faithfulness. If you were to keep the $600 deposit and not play, you would commit the sin of *"unlawful detaining of another's property"* and *"fraud"* (LC 113). Even if you refund the deposit, you are still breaching the moral duty of faithfulness in contracts, defrauding the couple of the specific arrangement and peace of mind they relied upon.

**The Ninth Commandment (The Sin of the "Unavoidable Conflict"):**
Your friend advises you to tell the couple you had an "unavoidable conflict" so they never know it was for money. This is a direct violation of the ninth commandment ("Thou shalt not bear false witness"). The Larger Catechism states that this commandment requires the *"preserving and promoting of the truth between man and man"* (LC 107). It expressly forbids *"all untruth, falsehood, and lying,"* as well as *"concealing the truth"* and *"supressing the truth"* (LC 108). You cannot ethically send that email. A lie disguised as a polite cancellation is a sin against God and a failure to love your neighbor.

**The Tenth Commandment (The Root of the Temptation):**
The desire to break your contract is rooted in covetousness. The tenth commandment requires *"full contentment with our own condition"* (LC 110). You are dissatisfied with the $600 you agreed upon because you see a larger sum of money. The Westminster Standards teach that true contentment in one's calling requires fulfilling your obligations without letting greed dictate your actions. 

**Counsel for the Gala:** You must decline the agency's offer. It is not a "career move" if it is built on a breach of faith and a lie. As Proverbs 22:1 (and the Westminster divines' understanding of it) reminds us, a good name and integrity are to be chosen over great wealth.

### 2. What to do about the Second Song

You loosely promised to "try" to learn a second song, but you have not had the time. Because you did not write it down and it was only a loose mention, the temptation is to simply ignore it, pretend you know it, or show up unprepared. 

**The Duty of Truthful Dealings:**
Even though the promise was informal and conditional ("I'll try"), the Larger Catechism requires *"truth and faithfulness in contracts and dealings"* (LC 112). You must not equivocate or suppress the truth. 

**Counsel for the Bride:** You must communicate honestly with the bride before Saturday. Tell her the truth: you committed to *trying* to learn the song, but you have not had the time to practice it to the standard you require for her wedding processional. Do not hide this out of embarrassment. Giving her the honest truth now allows her to make an informed decision (whether she wants you to play a simplified version, substitute a song you already know, or provide the original track). Honesty in this small matter fulfills your duty to promote the truth between you (LC 107) and prevents you from defrauding her of her expectations on the day of the event.

### Summary

The Shorter Catechism teaches that the chief end of man is *"to glorify God, and to enjoy him forever"* (SC 1). You cannot glorify God by breaking your word, lying to a bride, or coveting another man's money to pad your own income. 

Play the wedding. Keep your word. Tell the bride the truth about the second song. Trust God to provide for your career through integrity rather than through the deceitful advice of your friend.

Based on the moral reasoning taught in the Westminster Standards, here is the direct and honest guidance for your situation. 

**1. The Contract and the Price**
You owe the couple the exact dining table and six chairs for the exact price of $4,200. 

According to the Westminster Larger Catechism (Q. 113), the duties required in the eighth commandment ("Thou shalt not steal") include "truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and dealings between man and man," as well as "punctuality in performing of contracts." When you signed the written order for a fixed price without a price-adjustment clause, you entered into a binding agreement. The Larger Catechism (Q. 114) explicitly forbids "injustice and unfaithfulness in contracts." To unilaterally issue a revised invoice after the fact is a breach of contract and a direct violation of the eighth commandment. You cannot steal from your neighbor by demanding more money than was rightfully agreed upon.

**2. The Financial Losses**
You must bear the $1,400 loss yourself. 

When you quoted a fixed price, you assumed the business risk of material and labor fluctuations. The couple, in turn, assumed the risk of waiting for your specific craftsmanship and turning down other makers. Because you did not include a price-adjustment clause, you have no moral or legal ground to shift your business risk onto a couple who budgeted in good faith based on your word. The Standards do not permit you to defraud your neighbor to make yourself whole. You must absorb the $1,400 loss from your own pocket, treating it as the cost of keeping your word. If fulfilling the contract would cause you to go into genuine debt or ruin, you would be required to refund their deposit and restore them (LC Q. 113), but since you are merely losing your expected profit margin, the loss is yours to bear.

**3. The Timeline and "Mental Reservation"**
You must be completely honest about the Thanksgiving deadline, regardless of whether it was written in the contract. 

You noted that you only said you would "try" to have it done by Thanksgiving and that it was not in the written order. However, the Westminster Confession of Faith (24.5) explicitly requires that our promises and contracts be kept "in the plain and common sense of the words, without equivocation or mental reservation." You must not use the technical absence of a written date to deceive the couple or manage their expectations dishonestly. You owe them the truth about the curing finish and the actual timeline. You must communicate the delay openly and transparently, without hiding behind the loophole that the date wasn't written down.

**4. Rejecting the Supplier's Advice**
You must reject your supplier friend’s counsel. His advice to "revise the invoice" or "refund the deposit and sell to someone else" relies on the very sins forbidden in the eighth commandment. He is counseling you to engage in "unfaithfulness in contracts" and to use your leverage to commit "oppression" or "extortion" against a couple who is counting on you. The Westminster Standards do not permit us to do evil (break a just contract) so that good (profit) may come. The fact that "everyone is doing it" is morally irrelevant; human industry standards do not override God's moral law.

**Summary of Counsel:**
You owe them the furniture for $4,200. You must build the set, absorb the $1,400 loss as the cost of maintaining your integrity, and truthfully communicate the delayed timeline to them without making excuses. Your financial profit is entirely secondary to your strict duty to act with justice and faithfulness in your contracts.

Based on the moral theology of the Westminster Standards, particularly the Larger Catechism’s exposition of the Eighth and Ninth Commandments, here is the direct and honest counsel I would give you.

### 1. What You Actually Owe Them
You owe them the exact deliverables specified in the signed, fixed-price quote: the logo, menu, signage, and the print-ready packaging files. 

The Larger Catechism (LC 113) teaches that the duties required in the eighth commandment include **"truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and dealings"** and **"giving to every one their due."** A signed, fixed-price quote is a binding contract. You agreed to a specific scope of work for a specific price. The risk of miscalculating the hours required for the packaging dielines falls entirely on you, the contractor, not on the clients. 

The sins forbidden in the eighth commandment (LC 110) explicitly include **"unjust contracts," "breach of covenants,"** and **"withholding from others what is due."** To deliberately withhold the print-ready packaging files because they are tedious and unprofitable for you is a direct violation of this commandment. You are withholding what is due to them under the covenant you freely signed.

### 2. Regarding Your Friend’s Advice
Your friend’s advice is not just bad business; it is a profound moral failure. Suggesting that you secretly deliver a lesser scope of work because "they won't know the difference" relies on deceit and the exploitation of the vulnerable. 

This violates the Ninth Commandment. The sins forbidden here include **"concealing the truth"** (LC 112). Furthermore, the Larger Catechism (LC 122) teaches that the duties required in the ninth commandment include preserving the good name of our neighbor and dealing truthfully with them. Taking advantage of the bakery owners' language barrier and their technical ignorance of the design process to secretly shortchange them is a form of oppression. It is a grievous sin against the rule of love and the moral law. You must reject this counsel entirely.

### 3. What to Do About the Informal "Social Media" Promise
You mentioned you verbally promised to "maybe throw in a couple of social-media templates if it was quick." 

Morally, our word is our bond, but we must also look at the conditions of that word. The condition attached to your verbal promise was that it be "quick." Since it has proven not to be quick, the condition for including them in the fixed price has not been met. You are not morally obligated to ruin yourself financially on open-ended extra work. 

However, you cannot simply use their lack of English to let the promise fade away in silence. The Westminster Standards demand truth and faithfulness in all our dealings. You must communicate this to them honestly and respectfully, perhaps through a translator or a trusted intermediary if necessary. Tell them: *"I initially said I might be able to include social media templates if they were quick to make. They are taking much longer than anticipated, so I cannot include them in our original agreement. However, you are receiving every single thing listed in our written contract, including the complicated packaging files."*

### 4. What to Do About Your Financial Loss
You asked what to do about your losses. The short answer is: **you must bear them.**

The Westminster Confession and Catechisms do not provide a moral justification for defrauding a neighbor to cover one's own poor judgment or lack of foresight. Your financial loss is the direct result of your own error in estimating the work. Rather than compounding this error by sinning against the eighth commandment (stealing from an immigrant family by withholding what you promised), you must submit to this loss as the consequence of your own miscalculation. 

God calls us to be diligent, just, and content. You violated diligence and wisdom in your initial estimate; do not violate justice to fix it. Absorb the loss, repent of your lack of wisdom in pricing, and learn to estimate more accurately for your next client.

### Summary of Counsel
1. **Finish the work.** Deliver the logo, menu, signage, and the full print-ready packaging files exactly as written in your signed quote.
2. **Reject the deception.** Do not listen to your friend. Do not exploit the clients' language barrier.
3. **Communicate honestly.** Explain that the social media templates are taking too long to fulfill the "quick" condition of your verbal remark, but reassure them that the written contractual obligations are being met in full.
4. **Accept the loss.** Pay the price of your own poor estimation without seeking to recoup it at the expense of the vulnerable. 

If you do this, you will clear almost nothing in profit, but you will have kept your hands clean from theft, your tongue from deceit, and you will have shown justice and mercy to a small business that trusted you.

Based on the moral reasoning and theological framework of the Westminster Standards (the Westminster Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms), here is the direct, honest counsel you must receive. 

**Is the promise, and the marriage, still binding on you?**

Yes. The promise and the marriage are absolutely, unconditionally binding upon you. 

To understand why, we must look at how the Standards treat both the covenant of marriage (Chapter 24) and the nature of vows (Chapter 22). Marriage is not a mere contract based on the ongoing emotional satisfaction of the parties; it is a divine covenant (WCF 24.1, 24.5). Within this covenant, you made a specific, solemn vow to your wife to be her safe person and to help her toward recovery. 

The Westminster Confession is very clear on the binding nature of vows. Chapter 22, Section 6 states that once a man has vowed a duty, *"he may perform it, though it be a bitter task."* You promised to help her through her sickness. That it is harder than you imagined, and that it requires you to carry a heavy emotional burden, does not dissolve the vow; it is precisely the condition in which the vow must be kept. 

The counsel of your gym buddy—that you "signed up before you knew what you were getting" and that the promise was to "a version of her that doesn't exist anymore"—is not only cruel, it is a fundamental misunderstanding of the marital covenant, and it violates the Ninth Commandment by bearing false witness against your wife’s inherent worth and the binding nature of your vow. God did not condition the permanence of your marriage vow upon your wife remaining free of "baggage" or physical/mental affliction. You are bound to her, and you are bound to your word, just as you were on the day you made the promise.

**The Sin Already Committed in the Heart**

While you have not engaged in physical intimacy with the gym woman, the Westminster Standards teach that you have already begun to sin in your heart against the Seventh, Tenth, and Ninth Commandments.

1. **The Seventh Commandment (Chastity):** The Shorter Catechism (Q. 71) and Larger Catechism (Q. 137-138) teach that this commandment requires the preservation of chastity in body, mind, and affections, and forbids all unchaste thoughts, desires, and *occasions* of impurity. You are already finding "relief" in another woman and entertaining thoughts of a life without your wife. This emotional enmeshment is a breach of the Seventh Commandment. 
2. **The Tenth Commandment (Contentment):** The Larger Catechism (Q. 148) teaches that this commandment requires "a full consent of the mind with our lot" and forbids "murmuring, repining at our own lot." You are repining at your marriage and coveting a "lighter" alternative. You are discontented with the providence of God in giving you a wife who struggles with an eating disorder.
3. **The Ninth Commandment (Truth):** By listening to and entertaining the gym buddy’s slanderous rationalization of your betrayal, you are participating in an evil speaking that undermines the dignity of your wife (LCQ 140-141).

**What You Must Actually Do**

The Larger Catechism (Q. 153) reminds us that to escape the wrath and curse due to us for the transgression of the law, God requires faith, repentance, and the diligent use of the outward means. Here is your required course of action:

**1. Flee the Occasion of Sin Immediately**
The Larger Catechism (Q. 138) strictly requires the "avoiding of all occasions of uncanness." You must immediately terminate the inappropriate emotional intimacy with the gym woman. You must also distance yourself from the gym buddy. He is acting as a false counselor, leading you into sin and hardening your heart against your wife. As Proverbs (which heavily informs the Standards) warns, do not even walk near the door of the house of the adulterer. Cut the gym woman out of your life, and change gyms if necessary to remove the temptation.

**2. Repent of Your Heart Idolatry**
You must go before God in true, evangelical repentance (LCQ 76). You must confess that you have been seeking relief in the creature (the gym woman) rather than the Creator, and that you have been looking at your wife through a lens of selfish discontent rather than the lens of self-sacrificial, covenantal love. You must ask God for a renewed mind and a contrite heart.

**3. Keep Your Vow**
You must deliberately and actively choose to fulfill the promise you made. WCF 22.6 reminds us that God does not accept us as having kept our vows if we merely *meant* to; He requires the actual performance of the duty. You must become the "safe person" you promised to be. This means actively helping her toward recovery, refusing to weaponize her body, and offering grace rather than shame. You cannot do this in your own natural strength, because it is a "bitter task" to human flesh. You must rely entirely on the Holy Spirit and the grace of the gospel to empower you to love your wife as Christ loves the Church.

I'll address this as you've framed it: which of these two Lord's-Day problems is more heinous according to the Westminster Standards, so that you know which to take up first this week, and how to handle each.

---

## Breaking Down Each Case

### Case (a): The Scheduling Coercer

**Aggravating factors:**

1. **Targeting the vulnerable.** The affected workers are the lowest-paid seasonal employees — precisely the class the Standards' exposition of the whole law calls on those in authority to protect, not exploit.
2. **Coercion against a tender conscience.** Two of them are new believers who told her plainly they wanted to worship. The Westminster Confession (20.2) teaches that God alone is Lord of the conscience, and the Larger Catechism (Q. 117) makes sanctifying the Sabbath through worship a positive duty she is forcibly preventing.
3. **Hindering the means of grace.** They are kept from *public worship* — the very assembly WCF 21 calls the "great ordinance" God has appointed for spiritual welfare. She is not merely making their day less pleasant; she is cutting them off from the ordinary means of grace.
4. **Hypocrisy.** She keeps the day herself. This adds contempt of the second table's duties toward the neighbor to any surface-level pretense of piety.
5. **Economic leverage.** She uses the power of the schedule — and their dependence on their wages — to pressure them. This compounds the fourth-commandment violation with injustice and oppression under the sixth and tenth.

**The single most defining feature:** The use of positional power to coerce vulnerable new believers against their stated conscience, actively preventing their access to public worship.

---

### Case (b): The Open Profaner

**Aggravating factors:**

1. **Deliberate and settled habit.** This is not a one-time lapse under necessity or mercy (LC 117); it is a weekly, conscious choice to treat the day as common.
2. **Unnecessary work.** The projects are non-urgent and could plainly be done on another day, removing even the weak plea of "necessity" that the Standards allow.
3. **Public location and timing.** Done on the main streets as the church-going town walks to and from worship, the act is designed — or at least calculated to be heedless — of its offensive visibility.
4. **Leading others into sin.** His crew works alongside him, becoming participants in the profanation.
5. **Open scandal before the whole town.** The LC (following WCF 20.4) treats scandal — especially scandal given to the community as a whole — as seriously aggravating because it corrupts the public perception of God's law.

**The single most defining feature:** The deliberate, habitual, and fully public treatment of the Lord's Day as an ordinary workday — a brazen profanation intended for all to see.

---

## The Decisive Consideration in Ranking Them

Both are grave. But the Westminster Framework requires us to weigh the *nature* and *reach* of the sin:

- Case (b) is principally a **fourth-commandment sin** — a profanation and a public scandal. It is serious, and its open character multiplies its influence on the community's mind.
- Case (a) is a **multi-commandment sin**: it violates the fourth *in others*, violates the second (by hindering worship), violates the sixth (by harming the spiritual welfare of the weak), and violates the principles of justice and mercy owed to inferiors in authority (LC 125, duties of superiors). It is aimed at specific persons whose conscience she knows and overrides, and it uses their economic dependence as the lever.

The Westminster Standards consistently treat sins of oppression against the weak and sins that directly hinder the means of grace for those who desire them as among the most heinous categories. Hypocrisy — professing the day while denying its blessing to subordinates — compounds the offense under the first table as well. Case (b) is open rebellion, but it is one kind of sin. Case (a) is tyranny wrapped in personal pretense of piety.

**The decisive consideration:** Case (a) combines targeted oppression, coercion of a tender conscience, the prevention of public worship, and hypocritical use of economic power — aggravations across several commandments — whereas case (b), though publicly scandalous and habitual, is fundamentally a single-commandment profanation and public offense.

---

## Practical Guidance

**This week, take up (a) first.** Call the department head in. Require immediate correction: the three seasonal workers must be freed from that Sunday-morning shift without loss of hours or retaliation. The new believers must be accommodated in worship. You should make plain that using one's authority to coerce subordinates against conscience on the Lord's Day — when they are the weakest and most dependent — is not merely a scheduling problem but an act of injustice the council will not tolerate.

**Follow up with (b) the next week.** Call that department head in. Require that non-essential public works cease on Sunday mornings immediately. Address the public scandal: a municipal crew under his command should not be visibly treating the Lord's Day as a common workday in full view of every church-goer. If the work is truly non-urgent, it has no place on the Sabbath. Assign it to Saturday or weekday shifts.

---

RANKING: (b) < (a)

Here is the counsel I would give you, derived directly from the moral and theological reasoning of the Westminster Confession of Faith (WCF) and the Larger Catechism (LC).

**1. Do your ordination vows still bind you, and what of your friend’s advice?**

Your friend’s advice that you should "ghost it" because "half the session is checked out" is profoundly unbiblical and directly contradicts the Westminster Standards. 

According to the Westminster Confession of Faith (Chapter 22), vows made in a religious context—such as your ordination vows before God and the congregation—are made ultimately to God. Therefore, they must be "performed with like religious care and faithfulness." Your vow binds your conscience before God, not just before the people. 

Furthermore, your friend’s excuse that "nobody’s going to hunt you down" and "half the session is checked out" violates the moral reasoning of the Larger Catechism. In LC 147, the sins forbidden in the Ninth Commandment include "the breach of lawful promises." The fact that other elders are neglecting their duties does not excuse your neglect; two wrongs do not make a right, and you are judged by God’s standard, not by the collective apathy of your session. 

Are ordination vows a "suicide pact"? The Westminster divines would not use that flippant phrase, but they would affirm that you are not called to destroy yourself. However, the Westminster remedy for burnout is not to secretly break your vow by "fading away." Fading away without a word is a breach of your promise, a violation of the Ninth Commandment (truth and promise-keeping), and a sin against the "communion of saints" (WCF 26.2), which requires us to perform "private and public duties" for the good of the body. 

**2. If you need to leave, what is the right way?**

If your burnout and frustration have hollowed out your ability to serve, you are no longer in a position to faithfully discharge your "relations" (duties) as an elder (LC 135). But you must leave the office in a way that honors God and the church.

You do not have the right to unilaterally "ghost" the congregation you vowed to shepherd. Instead, you must go to the Session and, if necessary, the Presbytery. You must sit before your brethren, confess your inability to fulfill the duties of the office, and formally tender your resignation. 

If the Session tries to pressure you to stay and you know you cannot, you must hold your ground. If your departure causes friction or if your sudden withdrawal harms the flock, you make yourself subject to "church censures" (WCF 30) for the purpose of reconciliation and restoring order. But the right way is always through transparent, accountable communication. You must formally and verbally resign.

**3. Is the bookkeeping thing owed?**

Regarding your commitment to the deacons to "help look at the books when things settled down," you are not bound to take on the office of treasurer, but you are bound to handle this situation with Christian truthfulness.

First, you never formally took the vows of a deacon, nor did you sign a formal call to be treasurer. The office of deacon is distinct from the eldership, and without formal installation and vows, you are not bound by ecclesiastical oath to the diaconate. 

Second, your promise was conditional ("when things settled down"). The Westminster标准要求 (standards) require the "keeping of lawful promises" (LC 146). However, a conditional promise is only binding if the condition is met. Since things have not settled down (you are, in fact, deeply burnt out), the condition for your promise has not been fulfilled.

Therefore, you do not owe them your services as an unpaid CPA. However, the Ninth Commandment also requires us to avoid all that is "equivocal" or deceptive. You must not just let the deacons assume you will eventually do it. You must formally and politely withdraw your conditional offer, explaining that things have not settled down and you are unable to take on the responsibility. 

**Summary Counsel:**

Your friend is offering you worldly advice that prioritizes your comfort over your integrity and the well-being of the flock. As an elder ordained under the Westminster Standards, you are held to a higher standard of conscience. 

1. Do not ghost the church. It is a breach of your vow and a sin against truth.
2. Schedule a meeting with the Session immediately. Humbly explain your burnout and formally resign your office. 
3. Write to the deacons and clearly, honestly withdraw your conditional offer to look at their books. 

Step away from the offices if you must, but do so with your integrity intact, your vows honored, and your word kept.

Fellow Elders and Members of the Session,

You have tasked me, as chair of the worship-planning team, with drafting the new "Sunday Worship Enhancement Standards," and this evening the Session has voted these requirements into force. I am writing to inform you that I cannot and will not draft this document, nor can I implement it in our congregation. Because the Session has adopted these standards, I must formally dissent and resign my position as chair of the worship-planning team, and I ask you to consider my continued ordination as an elder. 

I gladly affirm your desire for order, reverence, and predictability in our corporate worship. Requirements such as a strict 10:30 a.m. start time, a fixed 75-minute order of service printed weekly, a 25-minute limit for the sermon in the final third of the service, and the strict limitation of sung worship to our approved psalter and hymns are entirely consistent with the Westminster Standards. These are lawful circumstances of worship, to be ordered by Christian prudence and the light of nature (WCF 1.6).

However, I cannot include or institute the mandatory "stations of encounter" (candle, anointing oil, holy water, and incense) or the annual "re-consecration rite" involving the touching of oil and the recitation of humanly authored decrees. To do so would require me to violate my ordination vows and the very Westminster Standards you and I have subscribed to. 

My reasoning, drawn directly from our confessional standards, is as follows:

**1. The Regulative Principle of Worship**
The Westminster Confession of Faith (21.1) explicitly states that "the acceptable way of worshipping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited by his own revealed will, that he may not be worshipped according to the imaginations and devices of men, or any other way not prescribed in the Holy Scripture." The physical stations of encounter, the use of incense and anointing oil outside of the biblical sacraments, and the annual re-consecration rite are not instituted by Christ in the New Testament. They are the imaginations and devices of men. We are expressly forbidden to add to the worship of God any ceremony or rite not prescribed in Scripture (WCF 21.1; 27.4).

**2. The Means of Grace and the Sacraments**
The requirement that we teach congregants that moving through these stations "opens the heart to receive grace" directly contradicts our confessional doctrine of the means of grace. The Westminster Standards clearly define the outward means of grace as the Word, sacraments, and prayer (LC 154). The sacraments are limited strictly to Baptism and the Lord’s Supper (WCF 27.4). Teaching that touching oil, water, or incense, or reading a meditation card, is a vehicle to "open the heart to receive grace" confuses and adds to the means of grace, which is a grave theological error. Furthermore, WCF 27.4 states, "There is not any other ceremony in the worship of God to be added." 

**3. The Liberty of the Conscience**
By voting these rites into force as "mandatory" for every service, the Session is binding the consciences of the congregation and the elders to human inventions. WCF 20.2 declares that "God alone is Lord of the conscience, and hath left it free from the doctrines and commandments of men, which are in anything contrary to his Word, or beside it, in matters of faith or worship." We do not have the authority from Christ to bind the consciences of God’s people to physical rituals that He has not commanded. 

**My Action**
Because you have voted these requirements into force, I am caught in a direct conflict between the majority vote of the Session and my subscription to the Westminster Standards. I cannot in good conscience draft the "Sunday Worship Enhancement Standards" document, as it would require me to codify and mandate unconfessional, unbiblical additions to worship. 

Furthermore, I will not lead the congregation in the "stations of encounter," nor will I participate in the "re-consecration rite." I will continue to preach, pray, and administer the lawfully instituted sacraments, but I must refuse to participate in or facilitate the invented ceremonies you have mandated. 

Therefore, I am stepping down as chair of the worship-planning team, effective immediately. I ask the Session to schedule a meeting to discuss my fitness for continued ordination, as I cannot submit to a decision that violates the Regulative Principle of Worship and the doctrine of the sacraments as taught in the Westminster Standards. 

I pray that the Session will reconsider this vote and return to the pure,Scripture-prescribed worship that our confessional standards so faithfully guard.

In Christ,

[Your Name]  
Elder and Former Chair, Worship-Planning Team

Based on the moral reasoning of the Westminster Standards, my direct counsel to you is this: **Yes, you are strictly bound to that price, and you must not invoke the force-majeure clause, raise the price, or sell the volume to the larger cafe.** You must honor the $11.50/lb price for the remaining two months of the agreement. 

Here is how the Westminster Confession of Faith (WCF) and the Larger Catechism (WLC) require you to reason through this situation:

**1. The Binding Nature of Your Promise**
You entered into a deliberate, fixed-price agreement to provide certainty to a struggling business. The Westminster Confession is very clear on the binding nature of promises and vows. WCF 24.2 teaches that a lawful commitment means a person "is bound to perform" what he has promised. You cannot use a "vague force-majeure line" as an escape hatch to negate a promise you clearly understood and freely made. To do so is to violate the sanctity of a vow.

**2. Justice and Faithfulness in Contracts (The Eighth Commandment)**
The Reformed tradition expands the Eighth Commandment ("Thou shalt not steal") far beyond literal robbery; it governs all economic and contractual relations. 
*   **The Duties Required:** WLC 118 explicitly defines the duties of the Eighth Commandment to include the practice of *"truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and dealings between man and man."* You made a promise for predictable costs; justice demands you keep it, even when it becomes financially painful for you.
*   **The Sins Forbidden:** WLC 113 explicitly forbids *"injustice and unfaithfulness in contracts"* as a sin against the Eighth Commandment. Breaking a contract to save your own profit margins, when you know it will harm the other party, is the very definition of contractual unfaithfulness. 

**3. The Prohibition of Evasion and Mental Reservation (The Ninth Commandment)**
Your distributor is tempting you to use a "vague" clause to break the contract, rationalizing that a literal, bad-faith reading of the fine print protects you. The Westminster Standards explicitly condemn this. WLC 112, expounding on the duties of truth (Ninth Commandment), requires sincerity and forbids all *"evasion, [and] mental reservation."* Using a hidden, vague syntactical loophole to evade the clear, mutual intent and spirit of an agreement is a form of mental reservation. It is a failure to deal "freely, clearly, and fully" (WLC 112) with your neighbor. 

**4. Covetousness vs. Promoting the Estate of Others**
Your friend is urging you to "maximize" and warning you that you are "leaving four dollars a pound on the table." The Standards address this greed directly. WLC 113 forbids *"covetousness, inordinate setting of the mind upon worldly things, [and] anxious and immoderate cares about getting."* You are being tempted to prioritize your financial optimization over your moral obligations. 

Furthermore, the Eighth Commandment does not merely require you to avoid harming your neighbor; it requires you to actively care for them. WLC 118 requires an *"endeavor, by all just and lawful means, to procure, preserve, and further the wealth and outward estate of others, as well as our own."* The small cafe has no cushion. If you break this contract, you will actively destroy their outward estate to improve your own. This is the exact opposite of what the catechism commands.

**Your Practical Course of Action:**
1.  **Honor the contract:** Continue to supply the cafe at $11.50/lb for the remaining two months. Take the hit; it is the price of your integrity and your word.
2.  **Reject the bad counsel:** Do not sell that volume to the larger cafe at the expense of the cafe that trusted your word. 
3.  **Speak the truth in love:** You are not required to suffer in silence or hide your financial reality. Speak honestly with the cafe owner *now*. Tell her plainly about the spike in your green-coffee costs and the reality of your margins. Do not do this to break the current contract, but to transparently prepare her for the *next* contract. 
4.  **Renew with justice:** When the six months expire, you are free to negotiate a new, honest agreement that reflects current realities, but you must do so based on a new, clear, and mutual consensus, not by weaponizing vague clauses to escape an old one. 

You are bound to that price because your word is your bond, and before God, your neighbor's economic survival cannot be sacrificed on the altar of your profit margin.

To give you counsel faithful to the Westminster Standards, we must look to the moral law of God as summarized in the Ten Commandments and expounded in the Larger and Shorter Catechisms.
